headline: Majors hold trend but momentum stalls as whales move coins onto exchanges and funding diverges between leaders and laggards.
paragraphs: The regime remains intact. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all trade above their 200-day simple moving averages, and Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, BNB all show golden crosses (the 50-day above the 200-day), a setup that normally carries weight. But the cross on XRP is broken, and Dogecoin and Cardano sit below their 200-day lines entirely, so this is not a unanimous picture: five of seven majors affirm the uptrend, two break it. That split matters because today's selling cut deeper than yesterday's. Bitcoin down 3.2% on the day, Ethereum down 4.6%, Solana down 5.4%, XRP down 9.7%. On the week, all seven are negative (Bitcoin down 5.2%, Ethereum down 3.2%, Solana down 6.0%, XRP down 9.0%, BNB down 6.9%, Dogecoin down 10.8%, Cardano down 10.3%). Yet on the month, six of seven are still up (Bitcoin up 19.3%, Ethereum up 29.1%, Solana up 31.9%, XRP up 19.6%, BNB up 21.1%, Dogecoin up 14.1%). The tension is clear: a month-long rally is being tested over the past week, and today the test deepened.

Momentum has stalled across the board, and the message is mixed with price action. Bitcoin's RSI-14 stands at 48.5, Ethereum's at 50.5, Solana's at 48.7: all neutral, nowhere near oversold but nowhere near momentum either. More telling, all seven majors show MACD below signal line, meaning the faster average has crossed below the slower one, a classic sign that acceleration is waning. BNB's RSI of 53.8 is the only one with real heat, yet even BNB's MACD is in bearish configuration. None of this says the trend is broken (price still above the 200-day), but it says the trend is resting and the buyers who drove the month-long rally have stepped back. Cardano and Dogecoin, the two already below their 200-day lines, show even lower RSIs (43.9 and 44.0 respectively), entering genuinely weak territory. The distribution of RSI readings suggests sellers have more conviction than buyers right now.

Positioning on derivatives tells a story of crowding and stress. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio sits at 1.77 on OKX, meaning for every short contract there are 1.77 longs: a 3-to-5 long bias is typical risk, this is stretched. Ethereum's ratio is 2.09, even more crowded. Solana's 2.33. But here is where it gets interesting: Bitcoin funding is positive at 0.26% per 8 hours (2.8% annualized), which means longs are paying shorts to hold the position; Ethereum funding has flipped negative at minus 0.22% per 8 hours (minus 2.4% annualized), shorts collecting premium. Solana funding is even more negative at minus 0.59% per 8 hours (minus 6.5% annualized), an unusually steep short premium. Meanwhile, Dogecoin's funding is rocketing: 1.0% per 8 hours, or 11.0% per year, one of the highest readings in the board. That coin's long-to-short ratio is 4.7, deeply one-sided. Over the last three hours, Bitcoin saw 4 times more longs liquidated than shorts (719,671 USD of long liq versus 177,613 of short). XRP liquidations are even more skewed: in just one hour of data, long liquidations dwarfed short ones 904,211 to 57,307. The crowd is long, funding is signaling pain for those positions on the bigger names, and the liquidation tape is printing bearish unwinds. This is the smell of leverage unwinding.

Whale behavior shows coins moving onto exchanges at a scale that warrants attention. Over the last 24 hours, 76.9 million USD of Bitcoin moved onto Binance, while 28.7 million USD of CRO moved off cryptocurrency.com. On the week ending September 15, 613 million USD of value moved onto exchanges in net terms. The prior week (September 8) saw 351 million onto exchanges. The week before that (September 1) saw 49 million. And the week of August 25 saw 1,199 million onto exchanges. The direction is consistent: whales are moving coins onto venues, a posture typically associated with distribution or hedging into rallies. Stablecoins total 310.3 billion USD, up 1.34% over the month, a modest increase in dry powder. Bitcoin ETF flows show a contradiction: 159.9 million USD net inflow on September 14 (yesterday), but minus 302.8 million USD over the five prior sessions. One day of inflow does not make a trend when five days moved the other way. Ethereum ETF flows are cleaner: 121.1 million USD inflow yesterday and 318.0 million USD inflow over five days, with two consecutive days in the same direction. The divergence between Bitcoin and Ethereum on the ETF side is notable: one is correcting a longer outflow, the other is building a buy. Fear and Greed reads 69 (Greed), at the high end of a 30-day range that bottomed at 31, suggesting the crowd still tilts toward risk appetite even as prices roll over and funding becomes dangerous for longs.

What to watch: Bitcoin's reclaim of 77,000 would suggest the pullback is shallow; a breakdown below 75,000 would test whether the 200-day line (still well above current price, implicit in the 'above SMA200' flag) attracts buyers or breaks. Ethereum's MACD flip to negative on a still-positive ETF flow window is a condition worth monitoring, a divergence between derivatives momentum and traditional-finance demand. XRP's loss of its golden cross is the most technical warning sign on the tape: the 50-day has likely fallen below the 200-day, turning what was a higher-low structure into a lower-low structure. Finally, the weekly whale flow into exchanges warrants a reversal signal: if the next week shows net outflow, that will suggest whales have finished distributing and are moving to offense. Until that changes, the posture remains defensive.
